title: TeamLease Services Ltd - 539658 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TeamLease Q4 FY26 operating revenue fell 2% QoQ to INR2,925 crore on NBFC insourcing, while PBT rose 30% YoY and FY26 EPS reached INR83.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined 2% sequentially to INR2,925 crore as the full-quarter effect of a large NBFC client's insourcing (about 20,000 associates moved to the client's payroll in Q3) hit volumes. Profitability held up: EBITDA grew 8% QoQ, PBT rose 30% YoY and PAT 22% YoY, helped by an INR143 crore income tax refund (including INR13.1 crore interest). Underlying PBT growth excluding the refund was about 20% YoY. Management said it is exiting about 10,000 low-margin headcount in Q1-Q2 FY27 and guided to EBITDA growth above 20% for FY27, with Suparna Mitra presenting her first call as MD and CEO.

financial_highlights.change: +30% YoY in Q4 (about 20% excluding tax refund); +36% FY26; general staffing PBT +11% FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR143 crore (incl. INR13.1 crore interest; INR106 crore principal for AY2024-25)

financial_highlights.change: from INR669 in Q1 FY26; FY25 close about INR665
taken in Q4 as exceptional item

segments.name: General staffing
segments.commentary: Closed Q4 with about 2.87 lakh associates, up over 4,500 QoQ; FY26 net headcount down about 5,500 but underlying adds about 14,000 excluding the Q3 transition. Contributes about 90% of group revenue; average salary about INR26,000 per month.

segments.name: Specialised Staffing
segments.commentary: Closed Q4 with 7,500 associates (net +1,000 YoY). PAPM up 17% and PBT up 15% YoY. GCC partnerships span over 110 GCCs, contributing about 60% of associate headcount and about 67% of revenue; 85 new logos added in FY26.

segments.name: Degree Apprenticeship (DA)
segments.commentary: Net addition of about 1,000 apprentices in Q4 and 10 new client logos; PAPM stable. Average apprentice salary about INR14,000 per month. Planned exit of low-margin headcount in Q1-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: HR Services (incl. EdTech)
segments.commentary: Full-year revenue up 22% and EBITDA up 23%; Q4 YoY looked weaker because EdTech billing shifted from Q4 last year to Q3 and Q4 this year. Added 42 universities in the quarter and 17 new in FY26.

segments.name: RegTech / HCM
segments.commentary: Combined digital and services MRR of INR3.6 crore per month. Management does not expect HCM to be a drag on group margins during FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA growth above 20% YoY in FY27 (stated as bottom-line/EBITDA target 'upwards of 20%'), without giving formal margin guidance.
Planned exit of about 10,000 headcount across staffing and DA in Q1-Q2 FY27 from revisiting low-margin mandates; management says no net margin impact because markups are very low.
Expects to end H1 FY27 and full FY27 with positive net headcount, supported by about 20,000 open positions at the start of FY27 (15-20% higher QoQ).
Enterprise segment margins expected to be broadly flat; staffing and DA margin expansion expected through FY27 via operating leverage.
Share buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at INR1,600 per share, funded from existing free cash.
capex_capacity: Investment in technology, talent and adjacencies flagged by the new CEO, but no quantified capex or timeline given; strategy still being finalised.
Digital backbone (compliance, payroll, associate engagement) lets the company run a larger associate book without linear core-team growth, per management.
Recruiter productivity up 20% YoY; cost-to-hire reduced about 20% YoY in FY26.
Shram Suvidha Portal expected to go live in 18-20 months as a central labour filings repository.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross joinees about 62,000, of which about 19,000 (31%) through internal hiring; about 15,000 (24%) first-time employees.
FY26 added about 120 new logos, about two-thirds under variable markup structures; about 70% of new general staffing mandates signed on variable markup.
BFSI hiring described as a one-off rotation; the unsecured retail credit cycle is still correcting. Consumer durables strong in Q4; quick commerce and e-commerce hiring concentrated in leaders.

Demand for traditional IT skills is weak; about 3-4% hiring on conventional tech skills, while AI, cloud, data and cybersecurity roles are rising. About 500-600 AI-skill hires in the last two quarters.
Global business revenue grew 200%, described as margin accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan to productise its proprietary placement, attrition and compliance data into AI tools?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna Mitra said productised offerings built on data plus on-ground execution are being actively worked on, with no timeline or financials given.

qa_highlights.question: Where do the EPFO and other legal notices stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani Dathi said a PF department demand of about INR180 crore relates to the 2000s PF trust surrender; the company has legal opinions and an NOC from PF authorities, and is confident of winning. GST and PF-related notices are also being contested.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for core staffing volumes and margins after the in-sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said in-sourcing was specific to one client and no broad trend has emerged; Enterprise is a volume play with flat margins, while staffing and DA margins should expand in FY27 via operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Can Specialised Staffing margins match higher-margin GCC peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna Mitra said bot models, RPO, hire-train-deploy and AI-led hiring are being added to lift GCC margins, with a multi-product approach planned.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount, PAPM and FY27 EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited open positions of about 20,000, FY26 PAPM of about INR665 closing versus INR689 in Q4, and FY27 EBITDA growth of above 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HR Services Q4 look weaker YoY, and what is the segment trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani Dathi said EdTech billing moved from Q4 last year to Q3 and Q4 this year, so full-year HR Services EBITDA is up about 22%. A separate call was offered for the segment EBITDA query.

risks_watch: Revenue decline from the NBFC in-sourcing and the planned exit of about 10,000 low-margin headcount in H1 FY27; watch whether the company holds positive net headcount at H1 end.
Quality of profit growth: Q4 PBT included a INR143 crore tax refund, so underlying PBT growth was about 20%, not 30%.
Labour code transition costs across the industry through FY27 as central and state rules are finalised, plus new regulatory changes.
Pending notices, including a about INR180 crore PF trust demand and GST matters, not provided for.
Geopolitical risks, including energy and petroleum price inflation and supply chain disruption, and uneven discretionary consumption.
Pace of new-CEO strategy rollout and any investment that could pressure margins; buyback execution at INR1,600 per share.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, operating leverage and the labour-code formalisation thesis, but cautious on near-term volumes. Management was evasive on specifics for the new strategy and on HR Services Q4 segment numbers, deferring them to a follow-up call.
key_quotes: We have the balance sheet to be bold.
We believe our stock is undervalued relative to the earnings power of the business and continued efficiency in cash conversion of the EBITDA.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA growth above 20% and positive headcount at end H1 and full FY27, backed by about 20,000 open positions (15-20% higher QoQ) and margin-accretive mix, but gives no quantified capex or capacity additions and no revenue growth guidance; Q4 revenue fell 2% QoQ and the brief gives no YoY revenue figure.
